observation_summary: The source map generation logic incorrectly treats original source line numbers as one-based, while the specification and other fields (generated line/column, original column) are zero-based. This leads to off-by-one errors in the generated source map output.
hypothesis: The source map generator implementation uses an incorrect indexing strategy (one-based instead of zero-based) for original source line numbers, causing a mismatch with the expected zero-based format.
prediction: The code responsible for calculating or storing the original source line number in the source map generator will be updated to subtract 1 from the line number, or the underlying data structure will be adjusted to store zero-based values.
experiment_rationale: The bug report explicitly states that original source line numbers should be zero-based. The failing tests show consistent off-by-one errors (e.g., expected 5 but was 4, expected 10 but was 9), which is the classic symptom of an indexing mismatch.
reasoning_summary: The defect is a procedural error in how the source map line number is calculated/stored. It is not a missing check (Checking), a wrong constant (Assignment/Initialization), or a design-level capability gap (Function/Class/Object). It is a computational logic error in the mapping algorithm, making Algorithm/Method the correct ODC type.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix might involve changing a value, the root cause is the logic of the mapping algorithm itself, not just an incorrect constant initialization.
There is no missing guard or validation; the logic is simply performing the wrong calculation.
